warnings: Factorial design with 2 CO2 levels × 2 N levels = 4 treatment combinations; data must be extracted separately for high-N and low-N subgroups
Nitrogen treatment affects foliar P concentrations directly - high N leads to lower P - so N level is a key covariate when interpreting mineral data
Table 1 reports means ± SE for 4 treatment groups: 350/high N, 350/low N, 700/high N, 700/low N - do not pool across N levels
P/N ratio is reported in mmol/mol units, not the same units as P concentration (µmol/g) or N concentration (mmol/g) - ensure correct units are used for each variable
Elevated CO2 consistently REDUCED foliar nutrient concentrations (N, P, Mg, K) - this aligns with expected dilution effect direction
High N treatment paradoxically caused LOWER P concentrations and lower P/N ratios - this is an antagonistic interaction, not a simple additive effect
Sample sizes are small (4-6 plants per treatment) and greenhouse compartments were replicated by 2 per treatment - the true independent replicates may be n=2 at greenhouse level
Field reference values are included in Table 1 but explicitly NOT included in statistical comparisons - do not use field values as control
Calcium showed marginal CO2 effect (P=0.10) and a significant CO2×N interaction (P=0.10) - interpret with caution
Soluble carbohydrate and starch data are only from morning samples (08:00-09:00) as noted in table footnote 4
Variables are expressed per unit total dry mass (not per area) - some photosynthesis parameters in Table 2 are in µmol g⁻¹ s⁻¹, not µmol m⁻² s⁻¹
WARNING: VAR-UNCLEAR - Variance type not clearly stated

recon.treatment_definition: Elevated CO2 at 700 µmol mol⁻¹ with either high N (0.3 mol N m⁻³) or low N (0.05 mol N m⁻³) irrigation
recon.potential_tc_confusion: None for CO2 assignment - labels are unambiguous. However, care must be taken not to confuse N treatment effects with CO2 effects when extracting pairwise comparisons. Each CO2 comparison must be made within the same N level.
recon.sample_size_source: All analyses were conducted with... measurements by 4-6 plants per treatment. Both the CO2 and N treatments were replicated by two greenhouses per treatment.
recon.factorial_structure: ["CO2 (350 vs 700 \u00b5mol mol\u207b\u00b9)", "Nitrogen supply (high N: 0.3 mol m\u207b\u00b3 vs low N: 0.05 mol m\u207b\u00b3)"]
recon.extraction_guidance: For meta-analysis of mineral concentrations, extract data from Table 1 only. Create separate extraction records for each mineral element (N, P, Ca, Mg, K) and for each N-level subgroup (high N and low N) separately, yielding 10 extraction records total (5 minerals × 2 N levels). Control values come from '350/high N' and '350/low N' columns; elevated CO2 values from '700/high N' and '700/low N' columns. Match by N level when pairing control and treatment. All values are means ± SE on a per-gram dry mass basis. Use n=4 as the conservative sample size estimate (paper states 4-6 plants per treatment). Note that the paper found significant CO2 effects on P (P<0.02), Mg (P<0.02), K (P<0.02), and N (P<0.01), but not Ca (P=0.10) or leaf mass per area. The N×CO2 interaction was not significant for any mineral. Chlorophyll should NOT be extracted as a primary mineral outcome. Do not extract data from Table 2 for mineral meta-analysis.
